## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible branchless blend with per-particle hash RNG and identity ordering can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
The ns/particle curve is FLAT across all tested N. At q=0.01, cost rises only from 25.091 ns/p (N=10000, just past L2 spill at N≈7710) to 26.959 (N=1000000, past L3 spill at N≈246723), then 26.411 at N=10000000 — a ~7% swing with no knee at either spill point. Death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape: q=0.5 lifts the baseline to ~33 ns/p at every N, still flat. The absence of any cache-spill knee confirms the algo is not memory-bound.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 2.71 GB/s at N=10000, q=0.01 — 21% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling. Bandwidth stays flat or slightly declines with N (2.71→2.52 at q=0.01) and falls with death rate (2.71→2.01 from q=0.01 to q=0.5). The algo is overhead-bound: frontend stalls dominate at 67–73% across all configurations, compute sits at 22–34%, backend stalls near zero. No regime transitions to bandwidth-bound.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize across particles. It used scalar SSE (`vmovss`, `vmulss`) with limited component-wise packed ops (`vmulps`, `vaddps`) on 4 floats within one particle. `vmovups xmm13,XMMWORD PTR [r9]` loads 16 bytes from a single particle; `vshufps`/`vinsertps` rearrange components before `vmulps`/`vaddps` blend them — within-particle, not cross-particle. No gather. The 383-instruction body includes hash-RNG chains (`imul`/`xor`/`shr`) and byte-granular LP2 stores (`mov BYTE PTR [rsi+rdi*1],r10b` with `cmovae` clamping). The instruction count and control flow (25 `cmp`, 12 `vucomiss`, 12 `cmovae`) explain the 70%+ frontend stalls: decode cannot feed enough µops to saturate compute or memory.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo peaks at 2.71 GB/s = 21% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling, frontend-bound at 70%+ stalls across every N and death rate, with no cache-spill knee. The per-particle hash RNG and byte-granular LP2 stores generate 383 instructions that starve the frontend, preventing any approach to the streaming ceiling regardless of churn.
